title: Chris Pratt confirms Savage Son adaptation for The Terminal List season 3
excerpt:
Chris Pratt confirms that The Terminal List season three will adapt Jack Carr's Savage Son.
The project continues the main series rather than launching another spinoff.
body_md:
Chris Pratt has confirmed the literary source for the third season of The Terminal List. Speaking while promoting his family film Way of the Warrior Kid, the actor revealed that the next season of the main Prime Video series will adapt Savage Son, the third novel in Jack Carr's James Reece series.

Pratt also clarified that the project is not another standalone spinoff in the vein of Dark Wolf. His comments distinguish the continuation of the central television narrative from the franchise's efforts to explore other characters and stories within the same fictional universe.

The decision follows the sequence established by the first two seasons. The original season adapted Carr's The Terminal List, while the second draws on True Believer. Selecting Savage Son for the third installment therefore preserves the order of the first three novels and gives readers a general indication of the material that may inform the next chapter.

Pratt plays James Reece, the central character of the series. The original television story follows a military veteran confronted with devastating events and difficult questions about whom he can trust. Its combination of conspiracy, personal conflict and action provides the foundation for the continuing narrative.

Published in 2020, Savage Son explores themes of hunting and survival, including the shifting relationship between hunter and prey. That broad premise suggests a different narrative emphasis from the earlier books without requiring readers or viewers to learn specific plot developments. It is important, however, not to assume that the television adaptation will reproduce every event or character arc from the novel.

The distinction between the main series and Dark Wolf is particularly relevant as the franchise expands. A spinoff can explore a different perspective or period without replacing the central storyline. Pratt's clarification establishes that the Savage Son adaptation belongs to the ongoing James Reece series.

From an editorial perspective, adapting successive novels gives the television production a framework for introducing new conflicts while retaining a recognizable protagonist. The different thematic emphasis of Savage Son may also offer opportunities to explore Reece's character in unfamiliar circumstances. Those possibilities remain interpretations of the source material rather than confirmed details about the television scripts.

The available report does not establish a filming start date, premiere date, episode count or complete cast lineup for season three. For now, the confirmed news is the selection of Savage Son and the continuation of the main Prime Video series. Further production announcements will be needed to establish how closely the adaptation follows Carr's novel.
